NBA Over/Under 2026-2027 Season

Created by Chester Ismay

Rooting guide →

Last updated at 2026-11-28 01:00 US Pacific time

Chance to win

Each day, the rest of the season is simulated 100,000 times. How good a team is comes from its record so far, pulled toward a preseason estimate (halfway between its Vegas line and DARKO’s preseason projection, counted as 20 games of evidence). Each simulation also draws how good the team really is, since a record is an uncertain guide; tested on 2021-22 to 2025-26, leaving that out made the chances too confident. Then every game left on the schedule is played between its two teams. Every simulated season is scored with the pool’s rules and tiebreakers. The dotted line is an even share.

How the simulations work

Each day’s chances come from 100,000 simulated finishes to the season. In each one:

  1. Estimate how good each team is. Its record so far is blended with a preseason estimate: the point halfway between its Vegas line and the wins DARKO projected before the season. That estimate counts as 20 games played at its pace (49.5 wins is a .604 pace, so it adds about 12 wins and 8 losses). Early on the preseason estimate dominates; by spring the record does.
  2. Allow for doubt about that estimate. Rather than treat the blend as exact, each simulation draws the team’s true win rate from a beta distribution centered on it, with the evidence counted at half weight. In a test on 2021-22 to 2025-26, a fixed rate gave teams 88% chances to finish Over that came true only 69% of the time; this step fixed most of that.
  3. Play out the remaining games. Every game left on the schedule is played between its two teams: the better team’s chance to win grows with the gap between the two drawn rates, and the home team gets the edge home teams have had (they won 55% of games in 2021-22 to 2025-26). One team’s win is the other’s loss, and who a team still has to play matters. Rest and injuries are not modeled. Games not on the schedule yet (the NBA Cup knockout rounds) are won at the team’s own drawn rate.
  4. Grade every pick and rank the entries. A team is Over if its final wins beat the line. Entries gain their wager on a right pick and lose it on a wrong one, then rank by points, number right, and 15s right. Entries still tied share the place.

A player’s chance to finish first (or top 4) is the share of the 100,000 finishes where they do. Every date reuses the same random draws, so day-to-day changes come from games played, not from simulation noise.

How it has done: run weekly on 2021-22 to 2025-26, readings of 70% to 90% ended in first place (the playoffs’ top seed) only 5 of 19 times, and players under 1% finished first about 4% of the time (Phil finished first in 2025-26 from 0.2%). Read big leads as less safe than they look.

Changed November 21, 2026: until then the preseason estimate was the Vegas line alone, and each team’s remaining games were drawn on their own, without opponents. In the same five seasons, adding DARKO ranked the players’ final places better in four of them, mostly in the first 20 games, when the line-only version did no better than chance. Playing out the real schedule then ranked them better again in four of the five. Neither change fixed the overconfidence in big leads described above. Every earlier date on these charts was recalculated. Picks are still graded against the Vegas line.

Chance to make the top 4

Chance of each place

Each player’s chance to finish in each place, from the latest day’s simulations, with the likeliest finishers first. Places 1 to 4 are the seeds for the Over/Under playoffs, so the line after 4th is the cutoff. Average place is the mean over all the simulated finishes. Players still tied after the tiebreakers split the places they cover.

Scenarios

The scenario explorer opens once 20 or fewer teams are still undecided, usually in mid-March. It lists every way those teams can finish and where each player ends up. 30 teams are open now.

By team

By week

Each team’s wins above (or below) the pace it needs to beat its Vegas line, as of each Sunday. Zero is exactly on pace; teams are ordered from furthest above pace to furthest below, with the line in parentheses. This plot is updated early each week with the previous week’s results (starting on Monday, October 26, 2026).

Over, clinched Over, on pace Under, on pace Under, clinched

By game number

Each team’s wins above (or below) the pace it needs to beat its Vegas line, after every game. A team on pace for exactly its line sits at zero; the line is in parentheses, and teams are ordered from furthest above pace to furthest below. Pale points can still change; solid points are clinched.

Over, clinched Over, on pace Under, on pace Under, clinched

Approaching win projection

  • Once a team passes its line, it has clinched OVER (solid blue).
  • Once a team can no longer reach its line in the games left, it has clinched UNDER (solid red).
  • Until then, pale blue or pale red shows which side it is on pace for.

The violet square is the number of wins the team would finish with at its current winning percentage, and the dotted violet line is that path from today. The horizontal line is the Vegas line, also shown in parentheses.

By conference

Playoff seeds are determined using the NBA’s official tiebreaker procedures. Seeds 1-6 earn direct playoff spots; seeds 7-10 enter the Play-In Tournament. When all tiebreakers are exhausted, alphabetical order is used as a stand-in for the random drawing specified in the rules.
